label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 1 · Question 2

hints.title: Write the intersection equation
hints.body: At an intersection the two expressions for y are equal. Collect everything on one side as a quadratic in x.
hints.recap: Substitution converts a line-curve intersection into one equation.
hints.pitfall: The question asks for no intersections, including no tangency.
hints.pause: Form the quadratic and identify its three coefficients.

recall.reminder: Substitution converts a line-curve intersection into one equation.

hints.title: Use the correct discriminant boundary
hints.body: Apply the discriminant condition for no real roots to your quadratic. Then solve the resulting squared inequality in m.
hints.recap: A quadratic with a nonzero leading coefficient has no real roots when its discriminant is negative.
hints.pitfall: A zero discriminant gives a repeated real root and must be treated separately.
hints.pause: Obtain the full parameter interval and check its endpoints.

recall.reminder: A quadratic with a nonzero leading coefficient has no real roots when its discriminant is negative.

solution:
1. Equate the heights. An intersection would satisfy x2+5x+6=mx−3, or x2+(5−m)x+9=0.

2. Exclude real roots. The leading coefficient is always 1, so no intersection means (5−m)2−36<0. Thus |5−m|<6.

3. Solve the bounds. −6<5−m<6 gives −1<m<11. The endpoints give tangency, which is an intersection, so they are excluded. Answer A.
knowledgePattern: Translate absence of line-parabola intersections into a strict discriminant range
